about: One-frame batch of answers delivered by ls::ugc::ModInfoCachedRequestSystem (macOS Update writes it) to the GUI (registry total 112, client only): a HashMap<ModItemInfoId, response> at +0 and a HashSet at +0x40.

evidence.says: Creator bg3.exe+0x3BEAC80 (AllocRaw 0x70) zeroes a HashMap (+0..+0x3F) and a HashSet (+0x40..+0x6F); destructor bg3.exe+0x3B7A220 destroys the map at +0 - bucket array of ls::HashSet

Creator bg3.exe+0x3BEAC80 (AllocRaw 0x70) zeroes a HashMap (+0..+0x3F) and a HashSet (+0x40..+0x6F); destructor bg3.exe+0x3B7A220 destroys the map at +0 - keys (written out member by member because the key is a struct)

Value storage at +0x30 (values: ls::ugc::ModItemInfoResponse, stride 0x150 - destructor FUN_143b7cf00 (shared with CacheModInfoSingleton) runs the PublishModInfo destructor FUN_1438b5d20 on value+8 for each key; same shape as QueryModInfoResultOneFrameComponent (u64, PublishModInfo +8, u32 +0x148)).
size of the value storage (ls::HashMap values are an uninitialised static array: pointer + count)

Destructor bg3.exe+0x3B7A220 runs the plain-key HashSet destructor bg3.exe+0x582AD0 on +0x40; macOS component destructor calls HashTable<ls::ugc::ModItemInfoID>::~HashTable(this+0x40): a HashSet of ModItemInfoID - bucket array of ls::HashSet

Destructor bg3.exe+0x3B7A220 runs the plain-key HashSet destructor bg3.exe+0x582AD0 on +0x40; key type assumed equal to the map's key (not checked) - keys (written out member by member because the key is a struct)

survey.live_reason: no live or captured instance: needs a situation that creates it
open_questions: The map's value storage is written as raw parts (pointer + count); value strides are known from the Windows destructors (see the Values row), the value structs are not declared. (ls::ugc::ModItemInfoResponse, 0x150 bytes, holding a net::PublishModInfo at +8)
Role of the HashSet at +0x40 (ids answered without data?).
survey.second_pass: The ModItemInfoID key is established from the Windows HashSet insert/find (bg3.exe+0x126FEA0 / bg3.exe+0x12705B0) and the macOS component destructor names the set at +0x40 as HashTable<ModItemInfoID>; the map's values stay raw parts.

fields.name: ModId
fields.evidence: Windows HashSet<ls::ugc::ModItemInfoID> insert bg3.exe+0x126FEA0 hashes the qword at +0 and the find bg3.exe+0x12705B0 compares it first (key stride 0x20); macOS ModInfoCachedRequestSystemHelper::RequestItemInfo(unsigned long long, Optional<Version>, bool, EHardwareType) takes the members in this order (mod id first).

fields.name: Version
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x126FEA0 hashes +8 only when the byte at +0x10 is set, and bg3.exe+0x12705B0 compares +8 only when both +0x10 bytes are set: the value of an optional (macOS Ensure<ModItemInfoID> identical) - the Optional<Version> argument.

fields.name: HasVersion
fields.evidence: has-value flag of the optional at +8 (bg3.exe+0x126FEA0 / bg3.exe+0x12705B0).

fields.name: RecursiveDependencies
fields.evidence: macOS modio::UGCManager::QueryMod (bg3_macos_x64+0x67995A0, called by RequestItemInfo(Guid, EUGCRequestType, u64, Optional<STDString>, bool, EHardwareType)) stores the bool argument at request +0xF4, and ProcessQueryItemResult (bg3_macos_x64+0x67A0130) passes that byte as the third argument of http::GetDependenciesRequestData(u64, u32, bool), which bg3_dx11.exe+0x38C0B30 writes as '&recursive=true/false'. The ModItemInfoID byte at +0x18 is that bool argument (ModInfoCachedRequestSystemHelper::RequestItemInfo(u64, Optional<Version>, bool, EHardwareType) takes the key's members in order; compared, not hashed): whether the dependencies fetched with the item info are resolved recursively.

fields.name: HardwareType
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x126FEA0 hashes the int at +0x1C and bg3.exe+0x12705B0 compares it: the EHardwareType argument of RequestItemInfo by order (enum not declared in Script Extender; 4 bytes).
